$comment: Named presets for the 12 Const + Pick columns of Format A (spec section 3).
These are constant across every run in the testing sandbox, so the UI keeps them
behind an 'advanced' disclosure instead of asking every time.

picklists.$comment: Active values from the Asset object describe, verified 2026-08-04. The app re-reads these live when connected and falls back to this list offline.

orderStatus.$comment: Spec section 9 traps 1 and 2. 'Confirmed' and bare 'Shipped' do not exist in this org.

catalogFilters.$comment: Which serialized-catalog rows the Families & SKUs picker shows for each family, keyed on Product_Series__c — the org's "L3 Product Series". That field is the only one naming a product line exactly; Device_Type__c calls every Driveri model AND Octo "Driveri". Driveri is declared as every device except the D810 series rather than a list of its seven current series, so a new D-series model appears without a config edit while staying disjoint from Octo. "Every device" is sfFamily Hardware — the STANDARD Product2.Family — not the custom L1_Product_Family__c, which does not exist on Product2 in staging and took that org's picker out entirely until 2026-08-15. The two are the same partition where both exist (testing: all 137 L1=Device rows are Family=Hardware, all 33 L1=Accessory rows are Family=Accessory), and a standard field cannot go missing between sandboxes. Haptic is declared on BOTH its series and its device type with match 'any' — see the haptic rule's own comment. Verified 2026-08-15, identical in both orgs: driveri 135, octo 2, dhub 2, dms 2, vbus 3, haptic 1 — of 170 catalog rows in testing and 168 in staging.

haptic.$comment: ACCAM1HAPTICMDL is one product the two sandboxes describe differently — testing has series HAPTIC and Product_Serialized__c No, staging has a BLANK series and Serialized Yes. Device_Type__c is HAPTIC in both and matches exactly one product in each org, so either signal identifies the family: match 'any'. The series stays listed even though staging's copy has none, because declaredSeries reads it to widen the query past the serialized gate — which is the only reason testing's copy, flagged No, is in the catalog at all.
